exposure: Concentrations of specific Human Milk Oligosaccharides (HMOs)
cohort: 78 breastfeeding Brazilian women who provided single human milk samples.
finding: Human milk oligosaccharide (HMO) concentrations exhibited high variability and were associated with maternal allergic disease, time postpartum, and infant's weight, weight gain, and sex; while maternal SeLe phenotype did not impact infant growth, higher concentrations of specific HMOs potentially protected against excessive infant weight gain.
